title: Symmetry Criterion for Van Hove Criticality at Non-Time-Reversal-Invariant Momenta
abstract:
At non-time-reversal-invariant momenta (non-TRIMs), time-reversal symmetry does not constrain the linear term of the band dispersion. Whether $
abla E$ vanishes is therefore determined entirely by the representation theory of the little group. For nondegenerate bands, $
abla E$ is forced to zero if and only if the vector representation $Γ_{\mathrm{vec}}$ of the little group does not contain the trivial representation $Γ_1$. When $Γ_{\mathrm{vec}}$ does contain $Γ_1$, $
abla E$ is not forced to vanish for any nondegenerate band; the classification instead depends on the multiplicity of $Γ_1$ in $Γ_{\mathrm{vec}}$. For degenerate bands, the Wigner-Eckart theorem and Clebsch--Gordan coefficients determine whether linear couplings vanish, with classification performed at the subband level. Applied to space group 225, the criterion explains why the $W$ point is critical for all nondegenerate bands, the degenerate $E$ bands are generically noncritical, and the $K$ and $U$ points host parameter-dependent criticality. Supporting phase diagrams reveal a two-tier hierarchy: symmetry enforces $
abla E=0$, while band parameters determine higher-order character. We extend this classification to all space groups hosting non-TRIMs in the single-group limit, providing a symmetry-dictated, parameter-independent framework for engineering Van Hove singularities in three-dimensional quantum materials.
summary: This paper develops a powerful group-theoretical framework to predict when Van Hove Singularities (VHSs) are guaranteed to occur at non-time-reversal-invariant momenta in electronic band structures. By analyzing the little group symmetry, it provides a parameter-independent criterion that dictates whether the band gradient must vanish due to fundamental symmetries of the crystal lattice.
main_problem:
The paper establishes a systematic, symmetry-based criterion to determine whether the band gradient ($
abla E$) vanishes at non-time-reversal-invariant momenta (non-TRIMs) in electronic band structures.
main_result:
The vanishing of $
abla E$ is dictated by the representation theory of the little group ($G_{\mathbf{k}_0}$); specifically, for nondegenerate bands, criticality is forced if and only if the vector representation ($\Gamma_{	ext{vec}}$) does not contain the trivial representation ($\Gamma_1$).
method: The analysis uses group theory (representation theory of the little group) applied to the band dispersion $E(\mathbf{k})$ near high-symmetry points, utilizing Wigner-Eckart theorem and Clebsch–Gordan coefficients for classification.
model_or_system: The study analyzes single-particle electronic band dispersions in three dimensions, modeled using a tight-binding framework applied to specific space groups (e.g., 225) under the single-group limit (no SOC).
key_observables:
Vanishing or non-vanishing of the band gradient ($
abla E$), which determines if Van Hove Singularities (VHSs) are symmetry-enforced critical points.
important_parameters: The crystal space group, the specific high-symmetry momentum $\mathbf{k}_0$, and the structure of the little group's vector representation ($\Gamma_{	ext{vec}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is strictly limited to single-particle band theory in weakly correlated, paramagnetic systems within the single-group (no SOC) limit.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate Brillouin zones marking TRIMs and non-TRIMs; tables summarize criticality ($
abla E=0?$) based on group symmetry for various points and bands.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general criterion using little group theory, applies it systematically to specific space groups (like 225) to classify VHS types at non-TRIMs, and concludes by providing a parameter-independent framework for engineering these singularities.
why_interesting:
While focused on solid-state band structure, the rigorous application of representation theory to determine fundamental physical constraints ($
abla E=0$) is highly relevant to understanding symmetry protection in quantum materials, which underpins many advanced topics in AMO physics and topological systems.

Panels: (a) face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with TRIMs Γ, X, L and non-TRIMs W, K, U; (b) body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice with TRIMs Γ, H, N and non-TRIM P; (c) body-centered tetragonal (BCT) lattice with TRIMs Γ, M, X, N and non-TRIM P; (d) body-centered orthorhombic (BCO) lattice with TRIMs Γ, X, S, R, T and non-TRIM W; (e) hexagonal (Hex) lattice with TRIMs Γ, A, M, L and non-TRIMs K, H; and (f) trigonal (Trig) lattice in the hexagonal setting with TRIMs Γ, A, M, L and non- TRIMs K, H.

FIG. 2. Flowchart for classifying VHS types at non-TRIM high-symmetry points. For nondegenerate bands (dim Γ = 1), the criterion proceeds in two steps: (i) check whether Γvec contains the trivial representation Γ1; if not, all 1D bands are critical; (ii) if yes, count the multiplicity of Γ1 in Γvec: multiplicity 1 ⇒noncritical, multiplicity 2 or 3 ⇒Non-VHS (excluded). For degenerate bands (dim Γ > 1), each subband is classified independently by counting the zero components of ∇Eα: 3 zeros ⇒ critical; exactly 2 zeros and 1 nonzero ⇒noncritical; otherwise (0 or 1 zero) ⇒Non-VHS (excluded). Dashed boxes indicate cases outside the scope of this work (generic points and TRIMs).
